title: [CQ-R11a] Guest check job start
definitionOfDone: A malformed or disallowed check frame exits 65, EOF before it 74, a missing workspace 66, and a missing moe-check account or session home 71; none writes a frame or starts a job. A non-empty protected list exits 65 until CQ-R11b. Shown by tests.

A recorder test with geteuid=lambda: 0 shows main() routing check to relay with ['/bin/sh', '-c', command], the moe-check identity with no supplementary groups, no agent socket, the network-namespace request and CQ-R11d's rlimits.

On Linux a real check job runs with exactly the allowlisted environment, cwd WORKSPACE, umask 077, NoNewPrivs 1 and CQ-R11d's rlimits in /proc/self/limits, and the workspace is re-owned without following a planted symlink. Shown by tests.

A drift test pins the supervisor's enforced identity and rlimits to CQ-R11d's CHECK_BOUNDARIES. Every pre-existing bridge test passes unchanged, and the verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Workspace re-own through directory fds, plus row K4 (DoD 3's symlink half).

reown(fd, uid, gid, prefix='') in guest-supervisor.py. check_job calls it on the root fd between the workspace open and session_home. ValueError gives 65; OSError gives 71.
- os.fchown(fd, uid, gid) on the directory itself. Then, for each name in os.listdir(fd):
  - path = prefix + name. If len(os.fsencode(path)) > MAX_PATH_BYTES, raise ValueError, checked before descending. Reuse R09's constant. It bounds depth (512 at most), recursion and open fds.
  - info = os.lstat(name, dir_fd=fd).
  - A directory is opened with WALK and a regular file with READ (R09's flags; O_NOFOLLOW, and O_NONBLOCK so a FIFO swap cannot block). Anything else (symlink, FIFO, socket, device) raises ValueError, before any chown of it.
  - os.fstat on the opened fd must show the lstat's (st_dev, st_ino) and the same type, and a regular file must have st_nlink == 1. Otherwise raise ValueError. A hard link would hand an outside inode to moe-check.
  - A directory recurses with path + '/'. A regular file gets os.fchown(fd, uid, gid). Close every fd in a finally.
- Never os.chown a path, so nothing can be followed. No WALK_LIMIT: the tree was root-materialized from a snapshot of at most 10,000 files in a fresh check VM, and no job identity has run yet. Say so in one comment.

K4, skipped on win32 and portable to macOS, uses step 1's harness. Its code wraps os.fchown with a recorder that appends (st_dev, st_ino, uid, gid) from os.fstat(fd) to an 'OWNED ' stderr line at exit, then calls the real fchown. Identity is injected as (os.getuid(), os.getgid(), None); fchown to yourself works non-root.
- Positive. The tree a.txt, bin/run (0755), src/lib/deep.c and empty/ reaches the recorder (42). The OWNED set equals the bigint lstat (dev, ino) of the root plus every entry, exactly once each, all with the injected uid and gid, and recorded before RELAY.
- Planted links, each 65 with empty stdout, no RELAY line, and no OWNED (dev, ino) of anything outside the workspace:
  - a symlink to an outside file;
  - a symlink to an outside directory holding a file (neither the directory nor its file is recorded);
  - a hard link to an outside file;
  - a FIFO.
- Bounds. A nested path of exactly MAX_PATH_BYTES bytes (read m.MAX_PATH_BYTES) reaches the recorder; one byte more gives 65.
- Failure. A recorder that raises PermissionError on its second call gives 71 with empty stdout and no RELAY line.
implementationPlan.note:
reown(fd, uid, gid, prefix=b'') landed in guest-supervisor.py. check_job calls it on the root fd after the WALK open and before session_home. ValueError and RecursionError give 65; OSError gives 71.

How reown works:
- It only ever calls fchown on fds, never os.chown on a path.
- Each entry gets an lstat first. A directory is opened with WALK and a regular file with READ; anything else raises ValueError before it is opened or chowned.
- fstat must show the lstat's (dev, ino) and S_IFMT, and a file must have nlink == 1.
- The R09 MAX_PATH_BYTES bound on prefix + fsencode(name) is checked before descending.
- No WALK_LIMIT, per the plan; the comment says why.

K4 (RED: nothing was re-owned, then GREEN):
- Positive: the 8 bigint (dev, ino) pairs of the root and every entry are each owned exactly once with the test uid/gid, before RELAY.
- 4 planted rows (symlink to an outside file, symlink to an outside dir, hard link, FIFO) each give 65 with no RELAY, no home and no outside inode owned.
- Path bound: exactly MAX_PATH_BYTES gives 42 and one byte over gives 65. These rows are guarded off on darwin because of PATH_MAX, per gotcha-local-runner-tests.
- A PermissionError on the 2nd fchown gives 71.

checkRun's owned field now collects every OWNED line.

Results: K1, K2 and K4 pass.

implementationPlan.description:
GUARD applies the check boundaries, plus row K3, a real job on Linux (DoD 3 and the DoD 4 drift).

GUARD in guest-supervisor.py, inside R10b's existing try, after its NoNewPrivs prctl and before the job's Popen:
- spawn = json.loads(sys.argv[3]).
- If spawn.pop('netns', False):
  - import fcntl, socket and struct;
  - os.unshare(os.CLONE_NEWNET), on the same main thread that forks the job;
  - bring up the namespace's own loopback, so local checks can bind 127.0.0.1: SIOCGIFFLAGS 0x8913, then SIOCSIFFLAGS 0x8914 with flags | IFF_UP (1), on an AF_INET SOCK_DGRAM socket, packing a 40-byte ifreq of '16sH22x' with b'lo'.
- For each name and value in spawn.pop('rlimits', {}), call resource.setrlimit(getattr(resource, name), (value, value)).
- Then job = subprocess.Popen(sys.argv[4:], **spawn).

Why GUARD, and not the job's child:
- GUARD runs a watch thread, so preexec_fn is out (R10b).
- Limits set here fail closed: any failure raises inside the existing try, GUARD exits 1 without '+', and relay reports 71, never a fabricated observation.
- Root GUARD is exempt from RLIMIT_NPROC at fork, and the job inherits every limit.

The netns and loopback branch runs only as root in the Linux guest. Tests skip it through check_job's netns=False seam, and K2 pins the request. Say in the comment that CQ-R13 certifies it on a real VM. An agent job's spawn carries neither key, so R10b's J-rows and every S/I/H row behave exactly as before.

K3 skips when off Linux ('the job probes read /proc').
- Busy-host skip. The test runs the job as the test user, so GUARD's fork and the job's fork count against RLIMIT_NPROC 2048 together with every task that user already runs; this box had about 1,184. Before running, sum Threads from /proc/<pid>/status over the test user's real uid. When the sum is >= 1792, call t.skip with that count as the reason.
- The harness, like R10b's J4:
  - reads its whole stdin into an os.pipe() whose write end it keeps open, and dup2s the read end onto fd 0;
  - writes probe.py into the workspace;
  - calls m.main(['check'], geteuid=lambda: 0, workspace=, sessions=, identity=(os.getuid(), os.getgid(), None), netns=False).
- The frame is {kind: 'check', version: 1, id: 'unit-1', command: 'python3 -I probe.py', protected: []}.
- dash exports PWD to its children and forks the last command, so the probe inspects the JOB itself, its parent os.getppid(): /proc/<ppid>/cmdline, environ, cwd (readlink), status (Umask and NoNewPrivs) and limits. It prints them as JSON.
- Decode stdout with guest-bridge.mjs's createFrameDecoder. Assert:
  - hello, output frames, and exactly one observation, with exit code 0;
  - cmdline == ['/bin/sh', '-c', 'python3 -I probe.py'];
  - environ deepEquals the six keys: PATH, HOME (the single home under sessions), USER and LOGNAME 'moe-check', LANG 'C.UTF-8', MOE_CHECK_ID 'unit-1';
  - cwd == realpath(workspace); Umask '0077'; NoNewPrivs '1';
  - for each CHECK_BOUNDARIES.resources.rlimits entry, the limits row named by the test's map {RLIMIT_CORE: 'Max core file size', RLIMIT_FSIZE: 'Max file size', RLIMIT_NOFILE: 'Max open files', RLIMIT_NPROC: 'Max processes'} shows that value as both soft and hard.
implementationPlan.note:
GUARD now applies the check boundaries before the job starts. It parses spawn = json.loads(argv[3]) inside the existing try, then, after the NNP prctl:
- if netns is set, it calls os.unshare(CLONE_NEWNET) and brings lo up with SIOCGIFFLAGS/SIOCSIFFLAGS on a '16sH22x' ifreq;
- it calls setrlimit(soft = hard) for each popped rlimit;
- it then calls Popen(argv[4:], **spawn).
An agent job's spawn carries neither key, and the R10b J and S rows pass unchanged.

K3 (Linux): a real job with netns=False and identity (uid, gid, None).
- It decodes hello, the outputs and one exit-0 observation, with empty stderr.
- From /proc/<ppid>, which is the sh job because dash forks its last command (re-verified here), it checks: cmdline is ['/bin/sh','-c','python3 -I probe.py']; the environment is exactly 6 keys; cwd is realpath(ws); Umask is 0077; NoNewPrivs is 1; and each CHECK_BOUNDARIES rlimit shows soft = hard in /proc limits.
- It skips if the user's thread count is >= 1792 (this box: 660).
- RED: 71, because GUARD handed rlimits and netns to Popen, which raised and so failed closed. GREEN after the change.

Ad-hoc evidence for the netns branch, outside the suite (/tmp/r11a-netns-probe.py):
- Under `unshare -r`, which makes the test user root in a user namespace, GUARD with netns True plus CHECK_RLIMITS started the job ('+'). The job saw interfaces ['lo'] only, bound and connected on 127.0.0.1, so lo is UP, and got ENETUNREACH (101) going outside.
- The netns=False control saw lo, eth0 and docker0 and reached outside.
- Not a suite row: it would push the diff past the 400-line limit, and CQ-R13 certifies the branch on a real VM.

Cleanup:
- The literal U+2028/2029/FEFF/E9 characters that my edit tool introduced were converted back to ASCII escapes. Both files are ASCII.
- The header and GUARD comments were compacted into additive lines.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Rejected these options:
1) Setting the rlimits in the job via preexec_fn, or a python exec stage. preexec_fn is unsafe with GUARD's watch thread. In a stage, a failure after '+' would show up as the check's own exit code (a fabricated code-failure), whereas GUARD fails closed to 71.
2) prlimit() after Popen. That races the job's first instructions.
3) Leaving lo down in the namespace. Every check that binds 127.0.0.1 would fail as code-failure, and CHECK_BOUNDARIES says interfaces ['lo'].
4) Validating protected entries now. They are unobservable until R11b, because every non-empty list exits 65, so mutants would survive.
5) os.chown(path, follow_symlinks=False) for files. Its lstat-to-chown window and hard links let an outside inode be re-owned; fd + fstat (dev, ino, nlink) closes both.
6) A WALK_LIMIT. The tree is root-materialized and finite, and the path bound already caps depth.

Verified on this box (Python 3.12.3, dash):

planningNotes.risks:
- NPROC. In non-root tests, GUARD's and the job's forks count against the test user's whole task count. K3 skips at >= 1792 rather than flake; production GUARD is root and exempt.
- A hard NOFILE below 4096 on some host makes setrlimit EPERM, giving 71 in K3. GitHub ubuntu runners have a large hard limit.
- R10b and R09 may land with different names. Adapt to them and note it, but keep R10b's J-rows and every bridge row byte-identical.
- The netns and loopback ioctl are runtime-untestable non-root. A wrong struct fails closed (71) and is caught by CQ-R13 on a real VM.
- Masking traps:
  - a malformed-row helper that respreads valid fields;
  - a recorder that writes to stdout;
  - an over-limit header WITH a body (then the read-order mutant survives).
- Orphans: spawnSync with timeout and SIGKILL; after sweeps, pgrep for sleep(600).
- forbiddenPatterns (__proto__, eval(, innerHTML) apply to test strings.
